titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §278: Ögödei's decree on the guards
about: Ögödei issues a long decree to regulate his guard, the night guard, day guards and quiver-bearers of Chinggis's time. It sets who lodges where, who may walk where, how the four shifts are staffed, the penalties for missing a shift, and the rank of his guardsmen over officers in the field.

sentences.t: Basa Ögödei Qaγan žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: Again Ögödei Qaγan decree when-becoming:
sentences.i: Again Ögödei Qahan issued a decree:
sentences.n: Read this section by its endings. Žarliγ bolurun (Ming 聖旨做時) is the formula “when the decree became”, which we render “issued a decree”: bol- “become” + the converb of time -urun. Basa (Ming 再) is “again”. The whole section is Ögödei's decree on the guards: kebteġül (night guard), qorčin (quiver-bearers), turγaγ̇ud (day guards), kešigten (men on a shift). Third-person commands end in -tuγai or -tügei, “let him …”, and I mark each one as it comes.

morph.gloss: Ögödei, a man's name (personal name) [(人)名]

sentences.t: Čiṅgis Qaγan ečige- dür min-u jabuγsad kebteġül qorčin turγaγ̇ud
sentences.l: Čiṅgis Qaγan father-at my having-gone-ones, night-guard quiver-bearers day-guards
sentences.i: The night guard, quiver-bearers and day guards of mine who went with Father Chinggis Qahan,
sentences.n: Čiṅgis Qaγan ečige-dür is “at / with Chinggis Qahan the father” (Ming 父行, -dür marks “with”); I take min-u (“my”, from bi) with the men who went, jabuγsad (Ming 行來的每, a plural past participle, “those who went”), not with ečige. The list is bare nouns; qorčin is qor “quiver” + -či + -n, and turγaγ̇ud is “day guards” (house rendering). Uncertain which noun min-u modifies.

sentences.l: all guardsmen-of conduct anew to-be-proclaimed decree when-proclaiming:
sentences.i: all the guardsmen's conduct — a decree newly to be proclaimed. In proclaiming it, he said:
sentences.n: I break the opening chain here: units 2 and 3 are one long noun phrase waiting for its verb, tuṅγaγ̇arun (“when proclaiming”, Ming 宣諭時). Kešigten-ü is “of the guardsmen” (kešig “shift” + -ten “those having”). Tuṅγun (Ming 作新 “make new”) I take as “anew”, from the same root as tuṅγaγ̇a-; the stem is uncertain. Daγ̇ulγaqui (Ming 宣諭) is “to be proclaimed”, stem inferred from the Ming.

sentences.t: "Qaγan ečige-jin žarlig(i)-jar urida ker jabuqun büleġei.
sentences.l: "Qaγan father-of decree-by formerly how going-ones were.
sentences.i: “By the decree of the Qahan, my father, as they used to go before,
sentences.n: Opening mark is Shiratori's. Žarlig(i)-jar is “by the decree” (Ming 聖旨依着: the instrumental -jar means “following”); ečige-jin is “of the father” (-jin after a vowel). Jabuqun büleġei (Ming 行的每有來) is “those who went, there was”, that is the habit of earlier times. Ker (Ming 怎生) is “how”. Here ečige-jin means Ögödei's father, Chinggis.

sentences.t: Edöġe mün josu-γ̇ar jabutuγai"
sentences.l: Now just rule-by let-go"
sentences.i: let them now go only by the rule.”
sentences.n: Josu-γ̇ar is “by the rule” (Ming 理依着). Jabutuγai is jabu- “go” + the optative -tuγai (Ming 者), “let (them) go”, here “let them conduct themselves”. Closing mark is Shiratori's. First of the many -tuγai commands.

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolurun:
sentences.l: saying decree when-becoming:
sentences.i: So he said, and issued a decree:
sentences.n: Keġen is keġe- “say” + -n, the converb that closes a quotation (Ming 麽道); it recurs after every quoted command. Žarliγ bolurun as in the first unit.

sentences.t: "Qorčin turγaγ̇ud uridu josu-γ̇ar
sentences.l: "Quiver-bearers day-guards formerly rule-by
sentences.i: “Quiver-bearers and day guards, as of old by the rule,
sentences.n: Opening mark is Shiratori's. Uridu is “formerly”; josu-γ̇ar “by the rule”, the same ending as before. The clause continues in the next two units; I break the sentence at the natural joints.

morph.gloss: day guard (inferred from the Ming 散班 'scattered shift') (noun) [散班(每)]

sentences.t: üdür mör mör-tür(i)-jen jabužu narataj-a
sentences.l: day post own-post-in going, day-having-in
sentences.i: going by day about their own duties, in the daytime,
sentences.n: Hard and uncertain. Üdür mör (Ming 日 職分) I take as “the day's duty”; mör-tür(i)-jen is mör “track, post” + -tür “in” + the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen “one's own” (Ming 自的行), so “in their own post”. Narataj-a (Ming 日有(的)行) is naran “sun” + -tai “having” + dative -a, “in the sunny time”, that is by day; I am not sure of the stem.

sentences.t: kebteġül-e žailažu γadana qonotuγai"
sentences.l: night-guard-to avoiding, outside let-lodge"
sentences.i: keeping clear of the night guard, let them lodge outside.”
sentences.n: Kebteġül-e (Ming 宿衞行) is the dative “to / from the night guard”; žailažu (Ming 躱着) “avoiding”, a converb -žu. So the day guards are to sleep outside the palace, away from the night guard. Qonotuγai is qono- “pass the night” + the optative -tuγai. Closing mark is Shiratori's.

to pass the night, lodge (verb) [宿者︀]

sentences.t: keġen žarliγ bolba.
sentences.l: saying decree became.
sentences.i: So he said, and issued the decree.
sentences.n: Keġen … bolba (Ming 麽道 … 做了) closes a command: “saying … became a decree”. The past -ba is the Ming 了.

sentences.t: Süni bidan-dur kebteġül qonotuγai.
sentences.l: Night us-at night-guard let-lodge.
sentences.i: “At night let the night guard lodge with us.
sentences.n: Shiratori prints no opening mark here; the quotation that closes at daruγalatuγai (unit 30) clearly begins at Süni, and I supply the opening mark in `i` only. Bidan-dur is the inclusive “we”, “at us” (Ming 咱行): by the ruler's side. Qonotuγai, -tuγai optative (“let … lodge”).

morph.gloss: we, inclusive (pronoun; stem bidan- before a case ending) [咱行]
night guard, those who lie down (from kebte-, 'to lie down') (noun) [宿衞]
to pass the night, lodge (verb) [宿者︀]

sentences.t: Eġüden-dür ger-ün horčin kebteġül baituγai.
sentences.l: Door-at, house-of around night-guard let-stand.
sentences.i: Let the night guard stand at the door and around the tent.
sentences.n: Horčin (Ming 周圍) is “around”, not qorčin. Baituγai is bai- “stand” + -tuγai; Ming 立者. Ger-ün is “of the tent” (-ün genitive, front-vowel).

morph.gloss: around, circuit (adverb or noun; Ming 周圍; not qorčin) [周圍]
night guard, those who lie down (from kebte-, 'to lie down') (noun) [宿衞]
to stand, be set up (verb) [立者︀]

sentences.t: Ordo-jin qoinaγ̇un uridaγ̇un kebteġül muqurituγai.
sentences.l: Palace-of behind-at front-at night-guard let-patrol.
sentences.i: Let the night guard patrol behind and in front of the palace.
sentences.n: Qoinaγ̇un and uridaγ̇un are “behind” and “in front” (Ming 後行 前行), with a locative-like ending -γ̇un that the Ming reads as 行 “at”. Muqurituγai (Ming 巡者) “let (them) go the rounds”; the stem is inferred from the Ming.

ending of uncertain force, read as a locative: at (Ming 行; back-vowel form)
night guard, those who lie down (from kebte-, 'to lie down') (noun) [宿衞]
to go round, patrol (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 巡) [巡者︀]

sentences.t: Naran šiṅgegsen-ü qoina süni jabuqun haran kebteġül barižu qonotuγai.
sentences.l: Sun having-set-of after night going-ones people night-guard seizing let-lodge.
sentences.i: After sunset, anyone going about at night — let the night guard seize him and keep him overnight.
sentences.n: Naran šiṅgegsen-ü qoina is “after the sun's having set” (Ming 日落了的後). Süni jabuqun haran is “people going by night”. Barižu qonotuγai is “having seized, let (them) lodge”; I read it as “keep overnight”, but qonotuγai after barižu is a guess from the Ming 拿着宿者. One long converb chain, left whole.

night guard, those who lie down (from kebte-, 'to lie down') (noun) [宿衞]
to pass the night, lodge (verb) [宿者︀]

sentences.t: Olon tarqaγsan-u qoina qonoγsad kebteġül-eče
sentences.l: Many having-dispersed-of after having-lodged night-guard-from,
sentences.i: After the many have dispersed, from those of the night guard who have lodged,
sentences.n: This sentence is hard; units 15 and 16 are read together and the sense is uncertain. Olon tarqaγsan-u qoina (Ming 多散了的後) is “after the many had dispersed”. Qonoγsad is a plural past participle, “those who lodged”; kebteġül-eče “from the night guard”.

morph.gloss: to pass the night, lodge (verb) [宿了的(每)]

sentences.t: busud dotoγši žöričen oroqun haran-i bariγsad kebteġül ekid an-u dalbaru čabčižu oγ̇ortuγai.
sentences.l: others inward ?-forcing entering people-OBJ having-seized night-guard heads their cleaving chopping let-go.
sentences.i: others, people who enter inward by force: the night guard who have seized them are to split and hack their heads, and let it go at that.
sentences.n: Very uncertain. Busud (Ming 別每) “others”; dotoγši “toward the inside”; žöričen (Ming 交慘 “cause misery”) I cannot read and take as “by force, recklessly”. The Ming gives 劈開 and 劈着 for dalbaru and čabčižu (both “cleave”), and 去者 for oγ̇ortuγai, so “let it go” may mean “let it pass”, “let it be so”; I give “let it go at that”. An-u (Ming 他的) stands after ekid, “their heads”, as in-ü follows its noun: the heads are those of the people seized. The grammar is clear (two converbs, then an optative) but the sense of the last word is a guess.

head (noun; the glossary's eki 'brain'; Ming 頭 'head'; uncertain) [頭(每)]

word uncertain (Ming 劈開 'split open'); taken as 'cleaving' [劈開]
to chop, hack (verb; stem inferred from the Ming 劈) [劈着]
to go (verb; stem uncertain, from the Ming 去 'go') [去者︀]

sentences.t: Süni jaγ̇aral keletü küġün ireġesü
sentences.l: Night haste word-having man if-comes,
sentences.i: If a man comes by night with urgent words,
sentences.n: Jaγ̇aral (Ming 忙) “haste”; keletü is kele “word” + -tü “having” (Ming 言語有的), “one having a message”. Ireġesü is ire- “come” + the conditional -ġesü (Ming 來呵).

sentences.t: kebteġül-dür keleležü ger-ün ümerēče kebteġül-lüġe qamtu baižu keleledütügei.
sentences.l: night-guard-to having-spoken house-of from-behind night-guard-with together standing let-speak-together.
sentences.i: let him tell the night guard, and, standing with the night guard behind the tent, let them speak together.
sentences.n: Kebteġül-dür is “to the night guard”; keleležü (kele- + -le- + converb -žü) “having spoken”. Ümerēče (Ming (北)行) is ümer “behind, back” + the ablative (“from behind”, as in the glossary); the glossators bracket 北 “north”, which would suit the back of a tent, so I put “behind the tent”. Keleledütügei has the reciprocal -dü- (“together”, Ming 共) plus -tügei: -tügei is the front-vowel form of -tuγai.

morph.gloss: behind, back (noun; the Ming writes 北 'north' in brackets) [(北)行]

sentences.t: Ordo ger-tür oroqu γarqu-ji Qoṅγortai, Širaqan-tan žasaγ̇ul kebteġül-lüġe qamtu žasatuγai.

sentences.i: As for those who go into and out of the palace tent, let Qongqortai, Shiraqan and the others, the jasa'ul, keep order together with the night guard.
sentences.n: Oroqu γarqu-ji is “entering (and) going out, (as object)”: two participles in -qu, the second with -ji (accusative). Širaqan-tan: -tan (Ming 等) “and the like”, uncertain. Žasaγ̇ul (Ming 官名, “an official title”) I leave as the title jasa'ul. Žasatuγai is žasa- “regulate” + -tuγai.

sentences.t: Elžigidei itegeltü böġetele žilda kebteġül-ün degeġün jabuqu bolun kebteġül-e bariγdalaγ̇a" keġen žarliγ
sentences.l: Elžigidei trusted-one while-being, in-the-evening night-guard-of over going when-being night-guard-by was-seized", saying decree
sentences.i: ‘Though Eljigidei is a trusted man, when he went about in the evening across the night guard's ground he was seized by the night guard,’ so ran the decree;
sentences.n: Shiratori prints only the closing mark (at bariγdalaγ̇a). This is an inner quotation inside the decree that began at Süni, so in `i` I supply an opening single quote and close it with a single quote. Itegeltü is itegel “trust” + -tü “having”; böġetele (bü- + -tele, “while, although”). Bariγdalaγ̇a is bari- “seize” + passive -γda- + a past ending; “was seized”. Degeġün (Ming 上) “over, across”; žilda (Ming 晩夕 “evening”) I read “in the evening”, as the glossary does.

sentences.t: busu ülü bolγaqu kebteġül itegeltü bi-že" keġen žarliγ bolžu
sentences.l: other not making night-guard trusted-one is", saying decree having-made,
sentences.i: ‘A night guard who makes no exception is the one to be trusted,’ so decreeing,
sentences.n: Again only the closing mark is printed; the single opening quote is supplied in `i`. Busu ülü bolγaqu (Ming 別不做的) is “who does not make (it) otherwise”, which I give as “makes no exception”: a literal reading, not certain. Bi-že (Ming 有也者): the stem bi- “is” (of bü-) + že “indeed”. Bolžu is a converb that carries the decree on into the next command.

sentences.t: kebteġül-ün toγ̇a bu asaγtuγai.
sentences.l: night-guard-of number not let-ask.
sentences.i: let no one ask the number of the night guard.
sentences.n: Bu + -tuγai is the negative command “let (them) not …”; Ming 休…者. Toγ̇a (Ming 數目) is “number”.

sentences.i: Let no one walk upon the night guard's station.
sentences.n: Saγ̇urin (Ming 坐次 “seating order”; 坐位 in unit 28) is “a place for sitting, a post”, from saγ̇u- “sit”. Degeġün (Ming 上) “upon”.

sentences.i: Let no one walk in the space between the night guard.
sentences.n: Žaγaγ̇un (Ming 其間) “between, in the interval”, the word žaγaγun “between” (the glossary’s form) with the ending as printed.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-ün degeġün jabuqun žaqaγ̇un jabuqun haran-i kebteġül barituγai.
sentences.l: night-guard-of over going-ones, between going-ones people-OBJ night-guard let-seize.
sentences.i: Anyone who walks upon the night guard's station or between them — let the night guard seize him.

sentences.n: Asaγqu küġün-ü (Ming 問的人的) is “of the man who asks”: a participle in -qu + a genitive. This unit and the next make one sentence; I break at the end of the list of things taken.

sentences.t: Kebteġül-ün saγ̇urin-u deġere ken ber bu saγ̇utuγai.
sentences.l: night-guard-of seat-of on anyone even not let-sit.
sentences.i: Let no one at all sit on the night guard's seat.
sentences.n: Ken ber (Ming 誰也) with bu is “no one at all”; saγ̇utuγai is saγ̇u- “sit” + -tuγai.

sentences.t: Kebteġül tuγ keġürge doro žida ajaγa saba asaratuγai.
sentences.l: Night-guard standard drum under lance cup dish let-take-charge.
sentences.i: Let the night guard take charge of what lies under the standard and the drum: the lances, cups and dishes.
sentences.n: Tuγ keġürge doro (Ming 旄纛鼓下) is “under the standard and drum”. Žida is the Ming 搶, which means “snatch”; I read it as a slip for 槍 “lance”. Ajaγa saba (Ming 器皿) “cups and dishes”. Asaratuγai is asara- “care for” + -tuγai.

sentences.l: Drink food-OBJ thick meat night-guard let-supervise"
sentences.i: Let the night guard supervise the drink and the food, the thick meat.”
sentences.n: Closing mark is Shiratori's: it ends the quotation I opened at Süni. Ideġen-i is “food” with the accusative. Ödgen miqa (Ming 稠肉 “thick meat”) is “meat in quantity”, or a stew; uncertain. Daruγalatuγai is daruγa (“governor”) + -la- “act as” + -tuγai: “let (them) supervise” (Ming 提調).
